title: Vegan Rosh Hashanah Vegetable Stew
subtitle: black-eyed beans, pumpkin, apple and quince
description: A festive stew that gathers the traditional Rosh Hashanah vegetables: black-eyed beans, apples, quince, pumpkin, honey and chard. Serve with pomegranate seeds and whole sesame seeds.

steps.text: Soak the chickpeas for 24 hours in plenty of water, changing the water twice. Drain, rinse, place in a pot, cover with water by 4 cm and cook for 30 minutes over medium heat until tender but still slightly firm. Drain and set aside.
Separate the chard stems from the leaves. Cut the stems in half crosswise and roughly tear the leaves.

Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a wide, heavy pot, add the sliced onions, the leeks (cut into 4 cm pieces) and the fresh turmeric and fry for about 7 minutes until golden and soft, stirring occasionally. Add the chickpeas and stir.

Layer the apples (peeled, cored, in 6 wedges), quince (peeled, cored, in 8 wedges) and black-eyed beans one on top of the other. Add the cinnamon sticks, baharat, ground turmeric (if not using fresh), pepper and salt and bring to the boil. Add the chard stems and leaves, top with the large cubes of pumpkin and the celery, add 1.5 cups water, drizzle with the honey, cover and cook for 30 minutes. Shortly before the end, preheat the oven to 170°C.
Transfer the pot to the oven and bake for 1.5 hours. Remove the lid and bake for another 30 minutes. Serve with pomegranate seeds and whole sesame seeds if you like.
